# `ota_begin`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Updater (firmware 9.75): start an OTA session against a target manifest.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ (firmware 9.75); partly INFERRED, see description |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.75, updater RPC handler @0x26530 (64-bit build), OTA manager; app 3.3.2 OtaService DTOs |

Firmware 9.75 (app 3.4.0) registers this method in the updater on TCP 4350, in both the 64-bit and 32-bit builds; firmware 9.31 registered none of the OTA methods (its updater had four). The handler clears the thread error code and calls the updater's single OTA manager. The OTA methods do not use the imager/guider secure-session layer (no such code in the updater); whether the JSON on 4350 is wrapped is not established. Firmware update is a high-risk operation; do not send this to a real device to test it. Starts an OTA session. The device compares the target manifest with its local manifest and works out which modules need an upgrade, then checks that send_modules is non-empty, has no duplicates, lists only modules of the target manifest, includes no module that does not need upgrading and misses none that does (error 102 with a text naming the problem). Packages received in an earlier session whose size and SHA-256 still match are reused. It creates the working directory, starts the session (stage pending) and starts the upgrade at once if every required module is already present. The reply gives the stage and the received and missing module names, and the device emits an OtaUpdate event with state working. A session in any non-idle stage refuses a new ota_begin with 524 (call ota_abort first, or ota_get_session to wait). The device then expects an ota_prepare_module for each missing module within a pending timeout of 15 s (READ, comparison of 15000 ms in the pending-receive check; the matching session-failure text is 'ota_prepare_module was not called within pending timeout').

Side effects: Creates an OTA session and a working directory; may start an upgrade at once.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"ota_begin"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Object params; the positional array form is not established. [READ] |
| `params.send_modules` | array<string> | yes | - | Names of the modules the client will send. MUST be non-empty, without duplicates, each present in target_manifest.modules, and MUST cover every module that needs upgrading and no module that does not. [READ] |
| `params.target_manifest` | object | yes | - | Target manifest. [READ] |
| `params.target_manifest.main_version` | string | no | - | Target main version string. [READ] |
| `params.target_manifest.modules` | array<object> | no | - | Target modules. [READ] |
| `params.target_manifest.modules[].name` | string | yes | - | Module name; must be a safe module name (the exact rule is not described here). [READ; rule detail unresolved] |
| `params.target_manifest.modules[].version` | string | yes | - | Module version string. [READ] |
| `params.target_manifest.modules[].sha256` | string | yes | - | SHA-256 of the module package file, 64 hexadecimal characters. [READ] |
| `params.target_manifest.modules[].size` | integer | yes | - | Size of the module package file in bytes; an integer greater than 0. Range: >= 1. [READ (range); unit INFERRED] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 102 | Validation failure: bad params or manifest, module not in the manifest or in send_modules, send_modules lists a module that needs no upgrade, or the manifest has no module that needs upgrading | `invalid parameters` |
| 107 | Missing params | `missing params` |
| 257 | The OTA temporary directory cannot be created | `cannot create directory` |
| 524 | Stage conflict or busy: the call is not allowed in the current OTA stage (text names the stage and, where relevant, asks the caller to ota_abort first) | `stage conflict` |

## Example

Request, request - Shape READ; all values invented:

```json
{"id":100,"method":"ota_begin","params":{"send_modules":["example_module"],"target_manifest":{"main_version":"9.99","modules":[{"name":"example_module","version":"1.0","sha256":"<64 hex digits>","size":1048576}]}}}
```

Reply, ok - Shape READ; all values invented:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"ota_begin","result":{"stage":"pending","received_modules":[],"missing_modules":["example_module"]},"code":0,"id":100}
```
